run.question: I have a slow query on the 'app-191-profile' index. Use the profile option to analyze this query and tell me the query type used: {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}}

report.summary: I ran the requested query {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} against the app-191-profile index with profile=true, supplying time_field=timestamp because the index maps timestamp and not @timestamp. The query type reported by the profile for the wildcard clause is MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper (term-level/multi-term query over the analysed terms of message), appearing as a child of a BooleanQuery inside a ConstantScoreQuery on shard [yxF_y55zS0q2BKHN3zahxw][app-191-profile][0]; a sibling TermQuery "message:timeout" is also present. The mapping shows message is text with no keyword sub-field. The profiled run itself was not slow (took 24 ms, 3 matching documents, single shard, no timeouts).

claims.text: With profile=true, the wildcard clause {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} is reported in shard [yxF_y55zS0q2BKHN3zahxw][app-191-profile][0] as a query of type MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper with description "message:*timeout*" (time_in_nanos 421206), nested as a child of a BooleanQuery (description "#message:*timeout* #IndexOrDocValuesQuery(indexQuery=timestamp:[1795452799000 TO 1795456399999], dvQuery=timestamp:[1795452799000 TO 1795456399999])") inside a ConstantScoreQuery.
The same profile lists a second child query of type TermQuery with description "message:timeout" (time_in_nanos 37789) next to the wildcard child within the BooleanQuery.
The index app-191-profile maps message as type text with no keyword sub-field, status as keyword and timestamp as date; no @timestamp field is listed in its mappings.

The profiled execution returned total 3 matching documents with took=24 ms and timed_out=false on 1 successful shard with 0 failed shards; the enforced timestamp filter limited the search to 2026-11-23T16:53:19Z–2026-11-23T17:53:19Z (source samples 17:48:00Z–17:52:00Z), and the index currently holds 6 documents in 5.8kb.

Because message is mapped only as text with no keyword or ngram sub-field, a pattern with a leading wildcard such as "*timeout*" cannot be resolved from an indexed prefix and its multi-term (MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper) form must expand against the analysed term dictionary — a plausible mechanism for slowness on a large corpus, though not demonstrated by this 6-document index.

The profile does not itself show a slow query: it completed in 24 ms with query phase ~1.8 ms on a single shard, matched 3 documents, and reported timed_out=false with no failed shards, so whatever slowness the user observes arises from different data volume or execution context than this sample.

Prefer a match query on message ("timeout") for full-text matching, or add a keyword sub-field and use term/match on it for exact-token filtering; only introduce a dedicated ngram/analyzer design if true substring search is required, instead of relying on the leading-wildcard "*timeout*" pattern.

gaps: One search call without time_field returned status error (INVALID_PARAMS, TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED, message that the matched indices map timestamp rather than @timestamp); that failed view is not citable, and the @timestamp absence is stated only from the mappings view.
No production-scale measurement was observed: the profile ran against an index holding 6 documents, so the user's actual latency figures and any pre-incident baseline remain unknown.

The profile carries gateway-injected min/max aggregations (opspilot_source_time_min, opspilot_source_time_max) and an extra TermQuery "message:timeout"; the instruction that added those clauses is not explained by the delivered evidence.
The search time filter is fixed to the last hour (2026-11-23T16:53:19Z–17:53:19Z), so the user's own slow execution could not be reproduced or compared.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no record of index setting, mapping or analyzer changes was available.
next_steps: Profile the same wildcard query against representative production-sized data to quantify per-shard cost before changing mappings.
If substring matching is required, plan a reindex with an appropriate analyzer/ngram or keyword sub-field and compare profiles against the match-query equivalent.
Confirm with the requester the exact latency measurement (client, endpoint, time range) that was observed as slow, since the profiled run returned in 24 ms.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.
